data.narrative: The student created a structured SkillSwap requirements analysis, identified explicit and implicit requirements, detected a cancellation policy contradiction, and proposed implementable solutions with tradeoffs.

dimension_scores.observation: Identified functional requirements, constraints, quality attributes, and hidden assumptions.
dimension_scores.evidence: Created artifacts/requirements/module-01-quick-pass.md and analyzed booking, payment, cancellation, and platform constraints.

dimension_scores.observation: Recognized relationships between cancellation, payments, refunds, and provider workflows.
dimension_scores.evidence: Identified that cancellation decisions affect payment flow, refunds, provider earnings, and provider settings.

dimension_scores.observation: Found ambiguity and contradiction risks before implementation.
dimension_scores.evidence: Detected conflict between provider-defined cancellation policies and universal refund rules.

dimension_scores.observation: Produced clearer requirement structure with stakeholder and requirement categories.
dimension_scores.evidence: Selected categorized matrix because it makes gaps visible and improves engineering estimation.

dimension_scores.observation: Handled requirement changes by proposing options instead of blocking.
Understood cross-feature impacts but needs more practice with system integration decisions.
dimension_scores.evidence: Connected cancellation changes with payment and provider dashboard impacts.

strengths: Strong at identifying hidden assumptions and contradictions in ambiguous requirements.
Good decision reasoning when choosing categorized requirements over a flat list.
growth_areas: Continue practicing dependency graphs and identifying critical paths between features.
data.recommendation: In the next module, focus on converting requirements into dependency chains and identifying blockers early.
